notes: Exact normalized subject-name matches with the same departmental flag are reused verbatim even if syllabus descriptions differ, per user instruction.

For non-name matches, reuse still requires departmental-flag and unit/topic alignment. An exact-name match with an incompatible departmental flag raises an error rather than silently generating a replacement bank.
Mid 1 scope is recorded from the first half of the ordered syllabus units; confirm against the official exam blueprint.
Generated question pools and theory answers are drafts requiring academic review.
TestsData contains only TestId, Questions, Options and Answers; mappings are held in test_index.
Theory rows use Options=[] and model answers in Answers; consumers must explicitly support both formats.
Project subjects are excluded completely and have no exam type banks or TestIds.
Exact-name duplicates with compatible flags reuse the source payloads verbatim.

This engine uses deterministic template generation for new subjects. Treat all newly generated questions and model answers as DRAFT until academic review; inspect stem validity, distractors, answer keys, syllabus scope, and difficulty.

subjects.name: Basics of Electronics Engineering
subjects.objective: This subject provides an opportunity for the students to get familiarized with all basic electronics components and study the characteristics of diode, transistors etc. Also student will get the ability to do simulation of corresponding circuits. The lab is designed for second semester students. Credits Earned: 3 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able 1. Develop the conceptual knowledge about the semiconductor and learn fundaments of terminal characteristics of PN junction diode and design /analyze fundamental circuits based on PN junction diode. 2. Identify limitation of diode and learning fundaments of transistor structure, types and behavioral characteristics and comparison of various transistor configurations. 3. Exploring the DC load line, biasing methods, comparisons in various amplifier configurations by understanding effects of change in Q-point by factors affecting stability. 4. Understand the various configurations of feedback amplifier, fundamental of FET devices and MOSFET. 5. Understanding and awareness about various type of component like LED, LDR, Varactor Diode, Photo voltaic diode etc. 6. Able to get aware about various types of available cable and connectors.

allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Common emitter amplifier.  Common collector amplifier  Multistage amplifier

allSyllabusUnits.topics:  JFET and MOSFET  Special purpose diode, Zener diode & it's application,  Photo diode  LDR  Photovoltaic Cell  Light Emitting Diode  Varactor Diode  Digital Display

allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Working principle of oscillator  Different types of oscillators: Hartley oscillator, Colpitts oscillator, Phase- Shift Oscillator, Wien Bridge Oscillator, Crystal Oscillator, FET Oscillator.

allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Cables: coaxial cable, twisted pair cable and fiber optic cable  Connectors: coaxial cable connectors, RJ-45, RS-232, HDMI connectors. Total 28.5 100 Syllabus for Diploma Engineering Information and Communication Technology

subjects.name: Electronic Practice
subjects.objective: This subject of ‘Electronics Practice’ is focused to provide the students with more hands-on experience and also enable them to develop and test simple PCB circuits. Selection of components, wiring, soldering, disordering, testing and troubleshooting, are some of the basic skills required by industry from any electronics engineering diploma holder. Students also need to develop enough learning confidence to complete entire project work related to various courses in subsequent higher level semesters. Hence, this course is designed to develop these vital skills required by the electronic industry through various laboratory experiences and strategies like mini-projects. Credits Earned: ​2 Credits
course_outcomes: ​After completion of this course, student will be able to ● Identify a particular component from the given group of active & passive electronic components ● Use of CRO and Function Generator for various wave generation and measurements. ● Will be able to analyze and interprets IC manual available in market ● Student will be able identify various hardware components and devices like diode, transformer, relay, Bread board ICs etc.. ● Will able to do soldering and de-soldering of general purpose components. ● Will able to create small project and trouble shoot same project.

Answers:
Model answer (8 marks)

**Meaning/purpose (2 marks):** Definition of unit is covered in “Units, Dimensions and Measurements”. A good answer should define its purpose, explain its main components or steps, connect it to Fundamental and Derived units, systems of units- CGS, MKS and SI, introduction to accuracy, provide a practical example and state how the result can be checked.

**Principles/steps (3 marks):** Explain the concept in logical order and relate it to syllabus areas such as Fundamental and Derived units; systems of units- CGS; MKS and SI; introduction to accuracy. State relevant components, formulas, assumptions or procedures.

**Application/example (2 marks):** Apply it to a concrete Applied Physics problem; identify the objective, selected method and expected outcome.

**Verification/conclusion (1 mark):** Check the outcome against the objective and mention a meaningful limitation, error source or trade-off.

**Meaning/purpose (2 marks):** Newton's first law says an object remains at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line unless a non-zero resultant force acts. Inertia is resistance to changing motion.

Questions: [8 marks] A student must apply number sets and laws of indices in a practical situation such as simplifying a product and quotient of powers with the same non-zero base. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply hcf and lcm of integers in a practical situation such as finding the HCF and LCM of 12 and 18. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply hcf and lcm of fractions and decimals in a practical situation such as finding HCF and LCM for 2/3 and 4/5 after simplifying the fractions. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply polynomial definitions and arithmetic operations in a practical situation such as simplifying (2x + 3) + (x − 5) and identifying degree. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.
Answers:
Model answer:
Number sets include natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, irrational numbers and real numbers, with each set having specific membership rules. For a non-zero base a, powers follow laws such as a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. These laws require attention to conditions such as non-zero denominators and the base not being zero for a^0. For example, 2^3 × 2^4 ÷ 2^5 = 2^(3+4−5) = 2^2 = 4.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
The HCF is the greatest positive integer that divides every given integer; the LCM is the smallest positive common multiple. Prime factorization is a reliable method: 12 = 2^2 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3^2. For HCF, take common prime factors with the smallest exponents, giving 2 × 3 = 6. For LCM, take each prime factor with the greatest exponent, giving 2^2 × 3^2 = 36. For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers.
